lead: Tesla / TSLA — hang onto your stock
smaller: Gold / GLD — is the record a buy or a sale?
Solana / SOL — the ETF makes it a brokerage trade
Shopify / SHOP — the Nasdaq move the crowd cheers
why_lead: Tesla stays the lead because it is still the best-supported trade on this date: down 26.37% over 20 sessions with a 5.27% bounce on 21 March, and the densest run of attention headlines in the window. Its catalysts changed after the 12 and 17 March leads: Musk's 21 March instruction to employees to hang on and the surprise all-hands meeting, the 20 March arson charges, Reuters' record trade-in exclusive and the 22 March call for the board to oust him. The 17 March loyalty framing and the Nvidia-on-Robinhood fact (14 March) are not repeated; the lead now tests the hold message against the trade-in data. The invalidation level is the 337.80 USD reference of 21 February.
why_smaller: Gold / GLD: a reversal rather than the 17 March '$3,000 and climbing' or the 19 March 'record while bitcoin falls' angle. Record prices are curbing Indian demand and Asian and Mid-East sellers are flooding jewellery markets (20-23 March), while GLD is up 2.86% over 20 sessions and spot has stalled over five.

Solana / SOL: a product event, two Solana ETFs coming (19 March), with Stocktwits buzz on the 2x SOLT (22 March) and a memecoin-cabal headline (23 March). It is distinct from the 4 March reserve-rally small. SOL is down 6.63% over 20 sessions and up 5.81% over five.

Shopify / SHOP: a company event, the move from NYSE to Nasdaq (20 March), with Stocktwits reporting that retail sentiment soared. The name appears in no earlier edition; SHOP is up 9.87% over five sessions and down 9.82% over 20.
considered_not_chosen: Quantum / IONQ: the 21 March lead already told the seal-of-approval story; the 23 March GTC panel item (n6170) is the same catalyst, and the buy-the-dip angle repeats the 7 March lead, so the small was dropped.

Rheinmetall / RHM: a fifth appearance (leads 5 and 10 March, smalls 12 and 13 March). The 23 March US-Ukraine and Russia ceasefire item (n4508) is a real new catalyst, but the Europe-rearming story is unchanged, so it is not repeated as a small.
Korean retail / leveraged tech: Bloomberg's 23 March headline (n6181) is fresh attention, but it gives no product detail, and the leveraged-ETF angle is the 21 March small.
Ether / ETH: a lagging-bitcoin debate with ETHA down 24.86% over 20 sessions, but the feed's attention is analyst commentary rather than retail flow.
Archer / ACHR: used as a small on 17 March; the 20 March FAA vertical-lift item (XTIA headline) is a sector catalyst but names no Archer attention.

Robinhood, Palantir, Nvidia, Oklo, Rocket Lab, Hims & Hers and Affirm: each already led or appeared as a small with no new catalyst that changes its story. Robinhood (11 and 18 March leads) and Palantir (6 and 21 March smalls) are the most repeated.
Lucid, GameStop and Opendoor: large five-session moves on the card, but no attention headline in this feed.
